title: 4月日銀利上げの確率急低下　市場予想30%、総裁どう反応
extracted_text:
利上げの有無が焦点になる日銀金融政策決定会合（27〜28日）まで残り2週間ほどとなったが、市場の利上げ観測が大幅に後退している。金利スワップ市場の取引動向から東短リサーチなどが算出した4月会合における0.25%の利上げ決定の確率予想値は14日午後3時15分時点で31%と、先週10日（57%）から大幅に低下した。

背景にあるのは、今になっても日銀から利上げを示唆する情報発信がないことだ。注目された13日の信託大会での植田和男総裁による挨拶（氷見野良三副総裁が代読）も「中東情勢がなお不透明な状況にあることを踏まえ、その帰趨（きすう）や、それが経済・物価・金融情勢に及ぼす影響を注視しつつ、経済・物価の中心的な見通しが実現する確度やリスクを点検していきたい」といった内容にとどまった。

むしろイラン情勢に関連した発言が目立ち、「中東情勢の緊迫が長期化した場合には、サプライチェーンへの影響を通じて、企業の生産活動に下押し圧力がかかるリスクもある」などと語った。

この時点で「予告」がないなら利上げは見送りだろうと市場参加者が見る背景には、日銀が2025年12月19日に前回の利上げを決めた際に、事前に丁寧な情報発信があった事実もある。

当時、植田総裁が「（次回の決定会合で）利上げの是非について適切に判断したい」と語り、政策変更を示唆したのは2週間以上前（14営業日前）の12月1日。市場の利上げの確率予想値は6割を下回る状態から約8割に跳ね上がり、その後、円滑な織り込みが進んだ。

今回の日銀の対応は25年12月と異なっており、海外市場関係者には4月の利上げ確率を国内市場より低く見る動きも出ている。「（利上げの）確率は20〜25%」と見るのは米金融情報コンサルタント会社のオブザーバトリーグループだ。

高市早苗首相は利上げに慎重姿勢とみられ、中東情勢の先行きも不透明な中、日銀は様子見を続ける可能性が高まっているとの趣旨の分析をする。

もっとも、24年に金利の引き上げを始めた日銀は、常に丁寧な情報発信をしてきたわけではない。24年7月の利上げ決定時は事前に十分な発信がなく、直前まで確率予想値が3〜4割程度にとどまっていた。次の25年1月の利上げも植田総裁が示唆したのは決定の9日前（7営業日前）だった。

従って、今回も現時点で利上げが完全に消えたと決めつけられるわけではない。特に為替相場の動向には注意が必要で、今後1ドル=160円を下回る水準に円安が進むなら、政権サイドも容認に傾く可能性は残る。

このため、今後も日銀の情報発信に注意を払っておく必要はある。

現時点で確定している機会は少ないが、当面の焦点は16日に開く20カ国・地域（G20）財務相・中央銀行総裁会議の後などに開かれそうな植田総裁の記者会見だ。利上げ示唆があれば市場にはサプライズになりそうだ。一方で「利上げ予想が大きく後退しているマーケットの空気をけん制しないなら、政策変更を見込む市場参加者はさらに減るだろう」（東短リサーチの加藤出氏）。

ただし、4月に動かなくても、金利引き上げの機会をうかがう空気自体は日銀内で消えないだろう。春季労使交渉での賃上げが日銀の想定通りの内容になっていることなどから、夏までには利上げを決めるとの見方がマーケットでも依然多い。

14日午後3時15分時点の市場で、6月までに利上げが決まる確率の予想値は76%、7月までの確率は106%になっている（100%を超えるのは0.25%を上回る利上げ予想が影響している場合）。

（編集委員　清水功哉）

translated_text:
With about two weeks remaining until the BOJ monetary policy decision meeting (April 27-28) where the focus will be on whether to raise interest rates, market expectations for a rate hike have significantly retreated. The probability forecast for a 0.25% rate hike at the April meeting calculated by Toshibin Research and others based on interest rate swap market trading trends was 31% as of 3:15 PM on the 14th, a sharp decline from 57% on the 10th last week.

The background for this is that there has been no communication from the BOJ indicating a rate hike even at this point. The speech by Governor Kazuo Ueda at the Trust Conference on the 13th (read on his behalf by Vice Governor Ryozo Himino) only stated that "given the continued uncertain Middle East situation, we will closely monitor its trajectory and its impact on economic, price, and financial conditions, while examining the likelihood and risks of achieving the central outlook for the economy and prices."

Instead, remarks related to the Iran situation were prominent, with statements such as "if the Middle East situation escalates and persists long-term, there is also a risk of downward pressure on corporate production activities through supply chain impacts."

The reason market participants view a rate hike as likely to be postponed if there is no "advance notice" at this point is also due to the fact that the BOJ had provided careful advance communication when it decided on the previous rate hike on December 19, 2025.

At that time, Governor Ueda had stated that he wanted to "appropriately judge whether to raise interest rates at the next decision meeting" more than two weeks earlier (14 business days earlier) on December 1st, indicating a policy change. The market's probability forecast for a rate hike then jumped from below 60% to about 80%, followed by smooth acceptance.

The BOJ's approach this time differs from December 2025, and overseas market participants are also viewing the April rate hike probability as lower than domestic markets. US financial information consulting firm Observatory Group sees it as "20-25%."

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is viewed as cautious about rate hikes, and with the future of the Middle East situation also uncertain, the analysis is that the BOJ is increasingly likely to continue watching and waiting.


However, the BOJ that began raising interest rates in 2024 has not always engaged in careful advance communication. At the July 2024 rate hike decision, there was insufficient advance communication, and the probability forecast remained at around 3-4% until just before. The next rate hike in January 2025 was also indicated by Governor Ueda only 9 days (7 business days) before the decision.


Therefore, it cannot be definitively concluded that a rate hike has completely vanished at this point. In particular, attention to exchange rate movements is necessary - if the yen weakens to levels below 160 yen per dollar, there remains potential for the administration to lean toward acceptance.


For this reason, continued attention to BOJ communications remains necessary.

While confirmed opportunities are limited at present, the immediate focus is on Governor Ueda's press conference expected to be held after the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors meeting on the 16th. If a rate hike is indicated, it would come as a market surprise. On the other hand, "if there is no pushback against the market sentiment that rate hike expectations have significantly retreated, market participants expecting policy changes will further decrease" (according to Toshibin Research's Izuru Kato).


However, even if action is not taken in April, the sentiment within the BOJ to seek opportunities for interest rate hikes will not disappear. With wage increases in the spring labor negotiations turning out as the BOJ expected, there remains strong market consensus that a rate hike will be decided by summer.

At the market as of 3:15 PM on the 14th, the probability forecast for a rate hike by June is 76%, and by July is 106% (the figure exceeding 100% is due to expectations for a rate hike exceeding 0.25%).


(Section Editor Shunji Shimizu)
